title: Moving into a Chinese-speaking city
summary: The practical language of a first month: a shower, a door code, a parcel locker, and a neighbour.
attribution: Original content authored for this project.

blocks.body: The first month in a Chinese-speaking city is usually a month of small physical problems rather than big ideas. You are hunting for warm water, a key, a shelf, and a place to stand out of the rain. The language you need is short, concrete, and repeating, which makes it some of the easiest Chinese to learn properly. Read each line below, then read it again covering the pinyin.

第一个月最难的不是语法，是生活。 Dì yī ge yuè zuì nán de bú shì yǔfǎ, shì shēnghuó. — The hardest part of the first month is not grammar, it is daily life.  我的房子在六楼，没有电梯。 Wǒ de fángzi zài liù lóu, méiyǒu diàntī. — My flat is on the sixth floor and there is no lift.  热水器只出热水，凉水要等很久。 Rèshuǐqì zhǐ chū rèshuǐ, liángshuǐ yào děng hěn jiǔ. — The water heater gives only hot water, and cold water takes a long time.  插座太少，我的电脑没有地方放。 Chāzuò tài shǎo, wǒ de diànnǎo méiyǒu dìfang fàng. — There are too few sockets and my laptop has nowhere to sit.  架子在门后面，钥匙我放在桌子上。 Jiàzi zài mén hòumian, yàoshi wǒ fàng zài zhuōzi shàng. — The shelf is behind the door and I keep my keys on the table.

大门有密码，我每天问同一个问题。 Dàmén yǒu mìmǎ, wǒ měi tiān wèn tóng yí ge wèntí. — The main gate has a code and I ask the same question every day.  门卫告诉我，一号门和二号的门不一样。 Ménwèi gàosu wǒ, yí hào mén hé èr hào de mén bù yíyàng. — The doorkeeper tells me that gate one and gate two are not the same.  楼下有快递柜，取件码是六个数字。 Lóu xià yǒu kuàidì guì, qǔjiàn mǎ shì liù ge shùzì. — Downstairs there is a parcel locker and the pickup code is six digits.  我第一次找不到，站在路边看了十分钟。 Wǒ dì yī cì zhǎo bú dào, zhàn zài lù biān kàn le shí fēn zhōng. — The first time I could not find it and stood by the road reading it for ten minutes.  现在我学会了：先看号码，再看方向。 Xiànzài wǒ xuéhuì le: xiān kàn hàomǎ, zài kàn fāngxiàng. — Now I have learned it: look at the number first, then at the direction.

邻居阿姨给我送过一次橘子。 Línjū āyí gěi wǒ sòng guo yí cì júzi. — The neighbour aunt once brought me oranges.  她说中文很快，我只听懂了三个词。 Tā shuō Zhōngwén hěn kuài, wǒ zhǐ tīng dǒng le sān ge cí. — She speaks Chinese fast and I understood only three words.  我慢慢说，她就笑了，说我的发音有意思。 Wǒ màn man shuō, tā jiù xiào le, shuō wǒ de fāyīn yǒu yìsi. — When I speak slowly she laughs and says my pronunciation is amusing.  住在这里以前，我以为最难的是汉字。 Zhù zài zhèlǐ yǐqián, wǒ yǐwéi zuì nán de shì Hànzì. — Before living here I thought the hardest part would be characters.  后来我发现，最难的是开口。 Hòulái wǒ fāxiàn, zuì nán de shì kāikǒu. — Later I found that the hardest part is simply opening your mouth.

blocks.title: Words for the first month
body: 门禁密码 ménjìn mìmǎ — door code
负一层 fù yì céng — basement level one
快递柜 kuàidì guì — parcel locker
取件码 qǔjiàn mǎ — parcel pickup code

blocks.title: Phrases that open doors
body: 我的钥匙忘在屋里了。 wǒ de yàoshi wàng zài wū lǐ le. — I left my key inside the flat.
热水器好像坏了。 rèshuǐqì hǎoxiàng huài le. — The water heater seems broken.
请问取件码在哪里？ qǐng wèn qǔjiàn mǎ zài nǎlǐ? — Excuse me, where is my pickup code?
能不能给我换一个插座？ néng bu néng gěi wǒ huàn yí gè chāzuò? — Could you change a socket for me?
我在三号门口等你。 wǒ zài sān hào mén kǒu děng nǐ. — I will wait for you at the door of number three.

blocks.body: Independent, unofficial reading material written from scratch for this project. It describes common everyday situations in general terms, is not taken from any commercial course, textbook, or official exam, and names no specific company, product, or service.
